physical_skill: Swing a toppled 18 x 16 cm panel upright about its bottom edge on a floor rib with one gripper and keep it there while the other gripper carries a loose chock into the 5.8 cm gap between panel and channel wall; release only once the chock holds the panel.
valid_shortcuts: Either arm may hold or chock; any grasp of the panel is allowed if its bottom edge stays in the channel (lifted no more than 5 cm, within 2 cm along the channel).
Placing the chock in the channel first and pushing the panel up against it is valid if the panel never falls after being stood up.
Standing the panel and letting go to fetch the chock lets it fall back (past 20 degrees after being within 6) and scores 0; holding instead of releasing scores 0 (fingers must be 2 cm clear).
distinct_from_nearest: Pending #2446 (another team) presses a leaning run of books upright and holds it while sliding a book into a 0.7 cm gap: same hold-then-insert shape but a different object set (a shelf of books vs a single panel in a floor channel with a loose chock) and the inserted object is the item being shelved, not a restraint. Accepted #46 locks a fallen see-saw platform with a lock before loading, a pinned mechanism rather than a free chock. Rejected #1324 levers a block and chocks it, #310 'leaning panel stabilization' and #1147 'free a panel from a leaning rack' are rejected; #2401 is our own rejected two-pane variant. Accepted #951 opens a locker with a leaning case. None has the same objects and same skill.
risks: Belongs to the saturated hold-one-thing-while-working-another family; reviewers may treat it as a variant.
Miniaturization: 0.45 kg bench-top panel on a deliberate pivot rib resembles the rejected #2401 objection; disclosed in context, fidelity and README limits.
Importance sources concern heavy stone slabs, not small panels.
